terms.gloss: I smell a rat, I suspect something
terms.grammar: impersonal, third person only: the person who suspects in the dative, the thing suspected as subject
evidence: Plaut. Ps. 1.5.7: id jam prīdem sēnsī et subolet mihi (Lewis & Short s.v. suboleō)
Ter. Ph. 3.1.10: Num quid patrī subolet? — Nihil etiam. (Lewis & Short s.v. etiam)
Traupman 106: I smell a rat, aliquid mihi subolet
terms.comment: Literally “it smells faintly to me”. Lewis & Short: only figurative, only in the third person singular, and ante-classical (Plautus and Terence).

phrases.latin: Num quid patrī subolet? — Nihil etiam.
phrases.english: Does Father suspect anything? — Nothing at all.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 106, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.: p. 316.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
